observations: Photo 0: an orange gas cylinder with brass valve and carrying handle, sitting among other cylinders (a red one in mesh wrap, a blue one, and a green-capped one) in a cluttered storage area.
Photo 1: the same orange cylinder from another angle, showing scuffed paint and a second orange cylinder stacked on a red one behind it.
Photo 2: close-up of an orange cylinder showing printed text '12,5' and the brand name 'REPSOL' with a logo, plus a barcode sticker; the valve area is out of frame/cut off at top.
No visible hydrostatic test stamp, manufacture date, or safety certification sticker legible in any photo.
Surface shows scratches, scuffed paint and some rust-colored marks near the base and handle in photos 0 and 1.
Multiple cylinders of different colors are present in the background; unclear which exact cylinder(s) are being sold.

claims.evidence: photo 2 shows printed '12,5' on the cylinder body
photo 2 shows 'REPSOL' branding, a Spanish/European LPG brand, consistent with a foreign-sourced cylinder
no test certificate, date stamp, or leak/pressure test shown in any photo

risks.risk: Valve or seal leaks, or valve does not hold pressure
risks.proof: a clip showing the cylinder connected to a regulator with a lit burner, or a soapy-water leak test on the valve
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / valve unverified

risks.risk: Cylinder past its hydrostatic test/certification date (safety and legal resale risk)
risks.proof: a close-up photo of the stamped test date ring near the neck or shoulder of the cylinder

risks.risk: Internal or under-paint rust/corrosion reducing structural integrity
risks.proof: photos of the base and seams with paint removed, or a weight/sound test clip
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic-only condition, risk of corrosion assumed

risks.risk: Cylinder may be empty or only partially filled despite 'gas cylinder' listing implying contents
risks.proof: a photo of the gas gauge or a weigh-in showing net gas weight

risks.risk: Ambiguity over which specific cylinder (of several shown) is actually for sale
risks.proof: a single clear photo of only the item being sold, isolated from other cylinders
risks.if_unproven: priced as the single orange 12.5kg unit shown in photo 2 only

proof_requests: Close-up of the hydrostatic test/certification date stamp on the cylinder neck or shoulder
Photo or short clip of the cylinder connected to a regulator and stove, showing gas flow/flame
Confirmation photo isolating exactly which cylinder is for sale, with all sides visible for rust/dents
A weight check or gauge reading to confirm gas is included and amount remaining
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a 12.5kg Repsol-branded LPG gas cylinder with visible brand text, so it can be priced at worst case (valve untested, no certification date visible, contents assumed empty) pending the listed proofs.
